items.explanation: 71-year-old man with atrial fibrillation documented 2025-08-22 (ICD-9 427.31). CHA2DS2-VASc 3 (hypertension, age 65-74, vascular disease: coronary atherosclerosis of native coronary artery). No anticoagulant in any current order or clinic medication list (most recent cardiology clinic note 2026-07-28 lists tamsulosin only). Guideline-recommended oral anticoagulation is absent.

Most recent ECG (101515306, 2022-04-27) shows sinus bradycardia at 58 bpm with QT 546 ms, QTc (Bazett) 535 ms. Amiodarone 200 mg daily is a QT watch-list medication and is current (order 2026-08-22, valid to 2027-01-05). Most recent potassium 4.1 mEq/L and magnesium 1.8 mg/dL (both 2026-02-14). QTc >= 500 ms on a watch-list drug requires prescriber review; no ECG has been obtained since 2022 despite continuing amiodarone.

Amiodarone 200 mg daily (a QT watch-list medication) was started at the cardiology clinic visit of 2025-11-10; it first appears in that visit's medication list. The 9/1/2025 memo applies (start before 3/1/2026), so an ECG was required within 30 days, i.e. by 2025-12-10. ECG 106885519 was obtained 2025-11-24, 14 days after the start, so the requirement was met.

Escitalopram 10 mg daily (QT watch-list) was started at the cardiology clinic visit of 2026-02-12 (first order and first appearance in the medication list). Start was before 3/1/2026, so the 30-day window of the 9/1/2025 memo applies: ECG due by 2026-03-14. ECG 101538691 was obtained 2026-03-08, 24 days after the start, so the requirement was met.

Citalopram 40 mg daily (QT watch-list) was started at the cardiology clinic visit of 2026-03-02; it is absent from the 2025-12-15 medication list and present from 2026-03-02. Start on/after 3/1/2026, so the revised memo applies: ECG required within 14 days, by 2026-03-16. ECG 104882441 was obtained at the 2026-03-07 visit, 5 days after the start, so the requirement was met.

Escitalopram 10 mg daily (QT watch-list) was started at the cardiology clinic visit of 2026-04-10. Start on/after 3/1/2026, so an ECG was required within 14 days, by 2026-04-24. The only ECG (107859369) was recorded 2026-04-29, 19 days after the start and 5 days after the deadline, so the monitoring was not completed within the required time.

Escitalopram 10 mg daily (QT watch-list) was started at the cardiology clinic visit of 2026-08-01; it is absent from the 2026-06-24 medication list. An ECG was required within 14 days, by 2026-08-15. The patient's only ECG is from 2025-12-25, before the start, and no ECG has been obtained since; the deadline has passed.

Escitalopram 10 mg daily (QT watch-list) was started at the cardiology clinic visit of 2026-08-10, so an ECG was required by 2026-08-24. The telephone note of 2026-08-25 records that the patient had an ECG at Northside Urgent Care on 8/18 (within the window) but the report was requested by fax and has not been received; there is no ECG for this patient in the chart. The outside tracing could have satisfied the requirement, so completion cannot be determined until the report arrives.

Haloperidol 2 mg twice daily (QT watch-list) was started at the cardiology clinic visit of 2026-09-15. Under the revised memo an ECG is required within 14 days, i.e. by 2026-09-29. No ECG has been obtained since the start (last ECG 2025-03-09), but the deadline is after the evaluation date of 2026-09-24, so the monitoring is not yet due.

At the cardiology clinic visit of 2026-09-01 Dr. Kessler documented a warfarin dose increase from 5 mg to 7.5 mg daily for a subtherapeutic INR of 1.6. The 3/1/2026 memo requires an INR within 7 days of a dose change made by a clinic clinician, i.e. by 2026-09-08. INR 2.3 was resulted on 2026-09-05, within the window, so the requirement was met.

Anticoagulation clinic telephone note of 2026-09-10 by the clinic pharmacist documents warfarin decreased from 5 mg to 4 mg daily per protocol for a home INR of 3.4. The 3/1/2026 memo requires a confirmatory INR within 7 days of a pharmacist dose change, i.e. by 2026-09-17. The most recent INR in the chart is 2.6 from 2026-08-22, before the change, and no INR has been resulted since; the deadline passed before the 2026-09-24 evaluation.

71-year-old woman with paroxysmal atrial fibrillation documented 2025-03-14 (ICD-10 I48.0) at the same admission as an embolic cerebral infarction. CHA2DS2-VASc 5: prior stroke (2), hypertension (1), age 65-74 (1), female sex (1). No anticoagulant is ordered; cardiology clinic notes through 2026-07-10 list only famotidine, metoprolol and carvedilol. Guideline-recommended oral anticoagulation is absent.

Outside-records summary of 2026-08-12 documents an admission 8/2/2026-8/5/2026 for upper GI bleeding from a duodenal ulcer (haemoglobin nadir 6.9, 2 units transfused) with apixaban held at discharge pending cardiology review. Nevertheless apixaban 5 mg twice daily was re-ordered at the 2026-08-20 cardiology clinic visit (valid 2026-08-20 to 2026-12-28) and is current, alongside aspirin and clopidogrel. Anticoagulation should not continue without the documented cardiology review of the recent major GI bleed.

At the 2026-07-15 cardiology clinic visit the plan was to switch from rivaroxaban to apixaban, but apixaban 5 mg twice daily (valid 2026-07-15 to 2026-12-26) was started while the rivaroxaban 20 mg daily order (valid 2026-07-15 to 2026-12-25) was left active; the visit medication list shows both. Two oral anticoagulants are therefore current as of 2026-09-24.

Cardiology clinic note of 2026-06-10 states 'ECG obtained today: normal sinus rhythm, rate 72'. Both 12-lead ECGs recorded the same day (107914094 at 17:13 and 103088543 at 19:36) show an irregularly irregular ventricular response with no discernible P waves at 139 and 144 bpm, i.e. atrial fibrillation with rapid ventricular response. Unspecified atrial fibrillation was also coded for the 2026-06-10 encounter. The documented rhythm and rate are contradicted by the same-day ECGs.

Heart-rate-rhythm observation of 2022-04-06 06:38 records 'Normal Sinus Rhythm'. The 12-lead ECG obtained the same day at 06:30 (100867733) shows an irregularly irregular rhythm (RR 0.32-0.62 s) without P waves at 131 bpm, i.e. atrial fibrillation; atrial fibrillation was also recorded four minutes earlier (06:34) and coded for that encounter. The sinus-rhythm documentation is contradicted by the same-day ECG.

Most recent ECG (108018814, 2023-10-08) shows sinus rhythm at 68 bpm with QT 478 ms, QTc (Bazett) 509 ms. Escitalopram 10 mg daily is a QT watch-list medication and is current (order 2026-04-23, valid to 2027-01-02). Most recent potassium 4.1 mEq/L and magnesium 2.1 mg/dL (both 2025-08-23) are normal. Per the 1/15/2025 QT monitoring memo a most recent ECG with QTc >= 500 ms on a watch-list drug requires prescriber review.

Most recent ECG (104821039, 2023-11-10) shows sinus rhythm at 70 bpm with QT 494 ms, QTc (Bazett) 534 ms. Citalopram 40 mg daily (a QT watch-list medication, and a dose above the 20 mg maximum advised with QT risk) is current (order 2026-05-29, valid to 2026-12-25). Most recent potassium 4.5 mEq/L (2026-01-21) and magnesium 2.1 mg/dL (2023-12-01). QTc >= 500 ms on a watch-list drug requires prescriber review.

Most recent ECG (106885519, 2025-11-24) shows sinus rhythm at 62 bpm with QT 514 ms, QTc (Bazett) 523 ms, up from 413 ms on the prior ECG of 2025-06-07. Amiodarone 200 mg daily is a QT watch-list medication and is current (order 2026-07-29, valid to 2027-01-05). Most recent potassium 4.4 mEq/L and magnesium 2.2 mg/dL (both 2026-04-20) are normal. QTc >= 500 ms on a watch-list drug requires prescriber review.

interpretations.explanation: Sinus bradycardia at 53 bpm with an upright P wave before every QRS. PR 176 ms, QRS 94 ms, QT 386 ms, QTc (Bazett) 363 ms. Frontal QRS axis about -8 degrees (normal). No bundle branch block and no AV block. Compared with the prior ECG of 2018-12-13 (sinus at 66 bpm, QTc 388 ms) there is no change in rhythm, conduction or QTc (difference 25 ms).

Sinus rhythm at 91 bpm with consistent P waves. PR about 185 ms (within normal limits), QRS 84 ms, QT 338 ms, QTc 416 ms. Axis about +2 degrees (normal). No bundle branch block. Prior ECG 2021-05-16 was sinus at 87 bpm, PR 136 ms, QTc 397 ms; no categorical change.

Sinus tachycardia at 112 bpm; RR intervals are essentially constant and a reproducible P wave (positive in II, negative in V1) precedes each QRS with a PR of about 180 ms. QRS 98 ms, QT 295 ms, QTc 402 ms, with ST depression and T wave inversion inferolaterally. Axis about +40 degrees (normal). Prior ECG 2022-07-04 was virtually identical (sinus tachycardia 115 bpm, QTc 402 ms); no change.

Sinus rhythm at 68 bpm with upright P waves. PR about 140 ms, QRS 92 ms, QT 478 ms and QTc (Bazett) 509 ms - prolonged, in a patient on escitalopram. Axis about +46 degrees (normal). No bundle branch block or AV block. The prior ECG of 2022-11-23 was sinus at 74 bpm with QTc 357 ms, so the QTc has increased by about 150 ms.

Sinus rhythm at 70 bpm with a P wave before each QRS. PR about 155 ms, QRS 106 ms (nonspecific intraventricular conduction delay, not meeting bundle branch block criteria), QT 494 ms and QTc (Bazett) 534 ms - markedly prolonged in a patient on citalopram 40 mg daily. Axis about +40 degrees (normal). The prior ECG of 2020-06-17 showed sinus tachycardia at 132 bpm with a rightward axis and QTc 461 ms; the QTc has increased by more than 60 ms.

Sinus rhythm at 66 bpm with consistent P waves; occasional slight RR variation only. PR 162 ms, QRS 98 ms, QT 353 ms, QTc 370 ms. Frontal axis about -51 degrees, i.e. left axis deviation (left anterior fascicular pattern) with deep S waves in II, III, aVF and V6. No bundle branch block. Prior ECG 2024-02-01 was also sinus with left axis deviation and QTc 396 ms; no change.

Sinus tachycardia at 121 bpm with regular RR intervals and a P wave before each QRS. PR 126 ms, QRS 90 ms, QT 302 ms, QTc 429 ms. Axis about +62 degrees (normal). No conduction abnormality. This is the patient's only ECG, so no comparison is possible.

Sinus tachycardia at 109 bpm with upright P waves. PR 116 ms, QRS 92 ms, QT 351 ms, QTc 475 ms (prolonged for rate). Axis about +34 degrees (normal). No bundle branch block or AV block. Only ECG available; no prior for comparison.
Sinus rhythm at 97 bpm with a P wave before every QRS. PR 106 ms, QRS 78 ms, QT 297 ms, QTc 379 ms. Axis about +1 degree (normal). No conduction abnormality. Single ECG; no prior comparison.

Irregularly irregular narrow-complex tachycardia at a mean rate of 145 bpm (RR 0.36-0.55 s) with no organised P activity - atrial fibrillation with rapid ventricular response. No measurable PR interval. QRS 102 ms, QT 288 ms, QTc 447 ms. Axis about -16 degrees (normal). The prior ECG of 2024-06-25 showed sinus rhythm at 81 bpm with PR 176 ms, so atrial fibrillation is new. QTc unchanged (difference 24 ms).

Sinus rhythm at 61 bpm. PR about 212 ms, i.e. first-degree AV block. QRS 134 ms with a broad monophasic R wave in I, aVL and V6 (no septal q, no S wave in V6) and a deep QS complex in V1-V3 - left bundle branch block. QT 445 ms, QTc 449 ms. Axis about -25 degrees (normal). The prior ECG of 2024-06-03 showed the same sinus rhythm with PR 218 ms and LBBB with QRS 134 ms, so neither the bundle branch block nor the AV block is new and the QTc is unchanged.

Sinus rhythm at 77 bpm with consistent P waves. PR 150 ms, QRS 76 ms, QT 400 ms, QTc 452 ms (mildly prolonged). Axis about +67 degrees (normal). No conduction block. Prior ECG 2020-02-02 was also sinus at 75 bpm with a low-amplitude inverted T wave and QTc 511 ms; the QTc has shortened by 59 ms, just short of the 60 ms threshold, so no change is reported.

Atrial fibrillation with rapid ventricular response, mean rate 139 bpm; RR intervals are irregularly irregular and no P waves are identifiable on signal-averaged analysis. No measurable PR interval. QRS 94 ms, QT 296 ms, QTc 450 ms. Axis about -12 degrees (normal). The prior ECG of 2024-08-18 also showed atrial fibrillation at 132 bpm (QTc 461 ms), consistent with the documented chronic atrial fibrillation; no change.

Atrial fibrillation with a slow, markedly irregular ventricular response, mean rate 53 bpm (RMSSD 0.44 s); no P waves are present and there is no measurable PR interval. QRS 112 ms (nonspecific intraventricular conduction delay). QT 385 ms, QTc 360 ms. Frontal axis about -36 degrees (left axis deviation). The prior ECG of 2024-09-04 also showed atrial fibrillation (81 bpm, QRS 116 ms, QTc 419 ms); no categorical change (QTc difference 59 ms, below the 60 ms threshold).

Atrial fibrillation at a mean ventricular rate of 99 bpm: the RR intervals are irregularly irregular (coefficient of variation 0.29) and no P waves can be identified, so there is no measurable PR interval. QRS 86 ms, QT 323 ms, QTc 415 ms. Frontal axis about -49 degrees (left axis deviation). This is the patient's only ECG; atrial fibrillation was coded at the same admission.

Sinus bradycardia at 52 bpm with a P wave before every QRS. PR 166 ms, QRS 94 ms, QT 417 ms, QTc 388 ms. Axis about +33 degrees (normal). No bundle branch block. Prior ECG 2023-05-22 was sinus at 57 bpm with QTc 346 ms; no categorical change (QTc difference 42 ms).

Atrial fibrillation at a mean ventricular rate of 87 bpm; irregularly irregular RR intervals with absent P waves and no measurable PR interval. QRS 92 ms, QT 369 ms, QTc 444 ms. Axis about +25 degrees (normal). The prior ECG of 2024-10-30 also showed atrial fibrillation at 65 bpm (QTc 433 ms); no change.

Atrial fibrillation with a slow irregular ventricular response, mean rate 53 bpm; no P waves and no measurable PR interval. QRS 92 ms, QT 414 ms, QTc 389 ms. Axis about +24 degrees (normal). The prior ECG of 2024-11-12 showed sinus rhythm at 69 bpm with PR 174 ms and clear P waves, so atrial fibrillation is new. QTc unchanged.

Sinus tachycardia at 121 bpm with constant RR intervals and a P wave before each QRS. PR 126 ms, QRS 92 ms (now narrow), QT 302 ms, QTc 430 ms. Frontal axis about +110 degrees (right axis deviation). The earlier ECG the same day (2024-12-05 01:33) showed a markedly widened QRS of 170 ms with a tall broad R wave in V1-V2 and terminal S waves in I and V6, i.e. right bundle branch block; this has resolved on the later tracing. QTc difference 46 ms, not a reportable change.

Irregularly irregular wide-complex rhythm at a mean rate of 96 bpm with no P waves and no pacing artefact - atrial fibrillation conducted with a marked intraventricular conduction delay (QRS about 160 ms, broad R in I and V6 with deep S in V1-V2). No measurable PR interval. QT 352 ms, QTc 445 ms. Axis about -17 degrees (normal). The prior ECG of 2024-12-03 (pacemaker check encounter) showed a regular wide-complex rhythm at 79 bpm with no atrial activity and no rate variation, i.e. ventricular paced rhythm; the current tracing shows intrinsically conducted atrial fibrillation, so the paced rhythm has resolved and atrial fibrillation is new.

Atrial fibrillation with rapid ventricular response at a mean rate of 152 bpm; irregularly irregular RR intervals with absent P waves and no measurable PR interval. QRS 86 ms, QT 290 ms, QTc 461 ms. Axis about +60 degrees (normal). The prior ECG of 2025-01-06 showed sinus rhythm at 86 bpm with PR 118 ms and perfectly regular RR intervals, so atrial fibrillation is new. QTc unchanged.

Sinus rhythm at 74 bpm with a P wave before every QRS. PR 180 ms, QRS 90 ms, QT 381 ms, QTc 423 ms. Axis about +35 degrees (normal). No bundle branch block or AV block. Only ECG for this patient; no prior comparison.

Regular wide-complex rhythm at 111 bpm with no discernible P activity and sharp high-frequency pacing artefacts immediately preceding every QRS (present in 100 percent of beats) - ventricular paced rhythm; the patient has a pacemaker/ICD in situ. No measurable PR interval. QRS 152 ms, QT 399 ms, QTc 543 ms. Frontal axis about +135 degrees (right). Conduction abnormalities are not separately reported because the wide QRS is pacemaker-generated. The prior ECG of 2020-11-03 was also a regular wide-complex (196 ms) rhythm without P waves at 109 bpm, i.e. already paced, so there is no new paced rhythm and the QTc is unchanged.

Sinus tachycardia at 111 bpm: the RR intervals are almost perfectly constant (0.51-0.55 s) and a small but reproducible upright P wave precedes each QRS with a PR of about 128 ms. QRS 78 ms, QT 297 ms, QTc 404 ms. Axis about +54 degrees (normal). The prior ECG a few hours earlier (2025-03-07 19:50) showed the same regular sinus tachycardia at 116 bpm (QTc 369 ms); no change.

Sinus bradycardia at 58 bpm with clear P waves. PR 108 ms, QRS 90 ms, QT 426 ms, QTc 420 ms. Axis about +57 degrees (normal). No conduction abnormality. Prior ECG 2025-03-08 was essentially identical (sinus 62 bpm, PR 108 ms, QTc 439 ms); no change.

Sinus rhythm at a baseline rate of 61 bpm with a single early beat and compensatory pause (RR 0.98, 0.98, 0.54, 1.37, 0.99 s); apart from this ectopic beat the rhythm is regular with a reproducible P wave (upright in II, negative terminal component in V1) before every QRS, so this is sinus rhythm with an atrial premature complex rather than atrial fibrillation. PR about 180 ms, QRS 104 ms, QT 388 ms, QTc 392 ms. Axis about -23 degrees (normal). Only ECG available; paroxysmal atrial fibrillation was coded clinically at this admission but is not captured on this tracing.

Sinus tachycardia at 102 bpm with a P wave before every QRS. PR 132 ms, QRS 94 ms, QT 338 ms, QTc 440 ms. Axis about +40 degrees (normal). No conduction abnormality. Prior ECG 2025-03-18 was essentially identical (102 bpm, QTc 433 ms); no change.

Sinus rhythm at 82 bpm with consistent P waves. PR 158 ms, QRS 106 ms (borderline intraventricular conduction delay, not meeting bundle branch block criteria), QT 377 ms, QTc 441 ms. Axis about +20 degrees (normal). Only ECG for this patient; no prior comparison.

Sinus bradycardia at 54 bpm. The P wave begins about 206 ms before the QRS onset, i.e. first-degree AV block. QRS 86 ms with a prominent R wave in V1, QT 393 ms, QTc 374 ms. Axis about +41 degrees (normal). No bundle branch block. The prior ECG of 2024-11-30 showed sinus bradycardia at 51 bpm with PR 184 ms and QTc 354 ms; PR prolongation has progressed slightly but there is no reportable categorical change (no change in rhythm, bundle branch block status or QTc).

Atrial fibrillation with rapid ventricular response at a mean rate of 134 bpm; irregularly irregular RR intervals, absent P waves and no measurable PR interval. QRS 94 ms, QT 287 ms, QTc 429 ms. Axis about +43 degrees (normal). The prior ECG of 2024-09-28 showed sinus rhythm at 59 bpm with PR 160 ms, so atrial fibrillation is new. QTc unchanged (difference 49 ms).

Sinus tachycardia at 104 bpm with regular RR intervals and a clear P wave before every QRS. PR 130 ms, QRS 102 ms, QT 391 ms, QTc (Bazett) 514 ms - prolonged. Axis about +18 degrees (normal). No bundle branch block. The prior ECG of 2025-06-20 showed sinus tachycardia at 147 bpm with QT 257 ms and QTc 403 ms, so the rate-corrected QT has increased by more than 60 ms.

Sinus rhythm at 69 bpm with consistent P waves. PR 144 ms, QRS 90 ms, QT 399 ms, QTc 427 ms. Axis about -25 degrees (normal). No conduction abnormality. The prior ECG of 2025-04-27 was also sinus at 60 bpm (QTc 406 ms) but with a negative lead I and positive aVR indicating arm-lead reversal on that tracing; rhythm, conduction and QTc are unchanged.

Sinus rhythm at 83 bpm with a P wave before every QRS. PR 140 ms, QRS 80 ms, QT 347 ms, QTc 409 ms. Axis about +51 degrees (normal). No conduction abnormality. Only ECG for this patient; no prior comparison.

Sinus tachycardia at 120 bpm; regular RR intervals with a consistent P wave merging into the preceding T wave. PR about 190 ms, QRS 98 ms, QT 280 ms, QTc 397 ms. Axis about +40 degrees (normal). No bundle branch block. The prior ECG of 2016-09-16 was also sinus tachycardia (108 bpm, QTc 396 ms); no change.

Atrial fibrillation with rapid ventricular response, mean rate 152 bpm; the RR intervals range from 0.29 to 0.58 s with no organised atrial activity, so there is no measurable PR interval. QRS 102 ms, QT 257 ms, QTc 409 ms. Axis about -4 degrees (normal). The prior ECG of 2025-09-12 showed sinus rhythm at 77 bpm (PR 144 ms) with a single premature beat, so atrial fibrillation is new. QTc unchanged.

Sinus rhythm at 66 bpm with consistent P waves. PR 152 ms, QRS 94 ms, QT 370 ms, QTc 387 ms. Axis about -27 degrees (normal). No bundle branch block or AV block. Only ECG for this patient; no prior comparison.

Atrial fibrillation with rapid ventricular response at a mean rate of 131 bpm; irregularly irregular RR intervals with no identifiable P waves and no measurable PR interval. QRS 88 ms, QT 294 ms, QTc 434 ms. Axis about +53 degrees (normal). The earlier ECG the same morning (2025-10-03 11:18) showed a perfectly regular rhythm at 97 bpm with a P wave before each QRS (PR about 196 ms), i.e. sinus rhythm, so atrial fibrillation is new. QTc difference 35 ms, not reportable.

Sinus rhythm at 77 bpm with a P wave before each QRS. PR 148 ms, QRS 96 ms, QT 319 ms, QTc 362 ms. Axis about +40 degrees (normal). No conduction abnormality. Prior ECG 2025-10-17 was sinus at 85 bpm with a more vertical axis and QTc 363 ms; no change.

Sinus rhythm at 73 bpm with clear upright P waves. PR 168 ms, QRS 94 ms, QT 362 ms, QTc (Bazett) 401 ms - now normal. Axis about +10 degrees (normal). No bundle branch block or AV block; this tracing confirms the same-day clinic documentation of sinus rhythm. The prior ECG of 2025-11-21 was sinus at 67 bpm with QT 504 ms and QTc 533 ms, so the QTc has fallen by more than 60 ms (marked interval normalisation).

Sinus rhythm at 62 bpm with a P wave before every QRS. PR about 172 ms, QRS 100 ms, QT 514 ms and QTc (Bazett) 523 ms - markedly prolonged with broad low-amplitude T waves, in a patient on amiodarone. Axis about +45 degrees (normal). No bundle branch block or AV block. The prior ECG of 2025-06-07 was sinus bradycardia at 47 bpm with QT 466 ms and QTc 413 ms, so the corrected QT has increased by more than 100 ms.

Sinus rhythm at 72 bpm with a P wave before every QRS. PR 138 ms, QRS 88 ms, QT 361 ms, QTc 396 ms. Axis about +19 degrees (normal). No conduction abnormality. Only ECG for this patient; no prior comparison.

Atrial fibrillation at a mean ventricular rate of 63 bpm; the RR intervals are irregular and no atrial activity survives signal averaging, so there is no measurable PR interval. QRS 118 ms (nonspecific intraventricular conduction delay, just below bundle branch block criteria). QT 380 ms, QTc 391 ms. Axis about +33 degrees (normal). The prior ECG of 2026-01-01 also showed atrial fibrillation (102 bpm, QRS 100 ms, QTc 363 ms); no categorical change.

Sinus rhythm at 73 bpm with regular RR intervals and a reproducible P wave before each QRS. PR 148 ms, QRS 104 ms, QT 360 ms, QTc 399 ms. Axis about +4 degrees (normal). No bundle branch block. Prior ECG 2026-02-17 was also sinus at 83 bpm (PR 136 ms, QTc 401 ms); no change.

Regular narrow-complex tachycardia at 107 bpm with a small but reproducible upright P wave before each QRS (PR about 150 ms) - sinus tachycardia. QRS 104 ms, QT 310 ms, QTc 413 ms. Axis about +10 degrees (normal). The prior ECG of 2026-02-24 showed sinus rhythm at 70 bpm with a slightly wider QRS of 122 ms that did not meet left or right bundle branch block criteria (S waves in both I and V6 without a terminal R in V1), so no bundle branch block change is reported; QTc 441 ms then versus 413 ms now, no reportable change.

Sinus rhythm at 101 bpm with clear P waves. PR 140 ms, QRS 94 ms, QT 321 ms, QTc 417 ms. Axis about +59 degrees (normal). No conduction abnormality. The prior tracing was recorded one minute earlier the same day and is essentially identical (101 bpm, QTc 416 ms); no change.

Sinus rhythm at 81 bpm with an upright P wave before every QRS. PR 184 ms, QRS 84 ms, QT 325 ms, QTc 377 ms. Axis about +34 degrees (normal). No bundle branch block or AV block. This tracing is consistent with the same-day clinic note documenting sinus rhythm. Only ECG for this patient; no prior comparison.
Sinus rhythm at 68 bpm with clear P waves. PR 134 ms, QRS 86 ms, QT 394 ms, QTc 420 ms. Axis about +53 degrees (normal). No conduction abnormality. Only ECG for this patient; no prior comparison.

Atrial fibrillation at a mean ventricular rate of 70 bpm; the RR intervals are markedly irregular (RMSSD 0.37 s) and no P waves are identifiable, so there is no measurable PR interval. QRS 90 ms, QT 383 ms, QTc 412 ms. Frontal axis about +125 degrees (right axis deviation) with deep S waves in the anterior precordial leads. Only ECG for this patient; atrial fibrillation was coded at the same admission.

Atrial fibrillation with rapid ventricular response, mean rate 140 bpm; irregularly irregular RR intervals without organised P waves and no measurable PR interval. QRS 96 ms, QT 292 ms, QTc 446 ms. Axis about +77 degrees (normal). The prior ECG of 2025-12-17 also showed atrial fibrillation at 118 bpm (QTc 466 ms), consistent with the documented chronic atrial fibrillation; no change.

Regular rhythm at 69 bpm with a reproducible atrial deflection before every QRS and a PR of about 138 ms - sinus rhythm. QRS 94 ms, QT 355 ms, QTc 382 ms. The frontal plane axis computed from leads I and aVF is about -175 degrees, i.e. an extreme (northwest) axis: lead I shows a deep S wave and aVR is dominantly positive while the praecordial R wave progression is normal, a pattern that strongly suggests right/left arm lead reversal rather than true dextrocardia - the limb lead placement should be checked. No bundle branch block or AV block. Only ECG for this patient; no prior comparison.

Atrial fibrillation with rapid ventricular response at a mean rate of 144 bpm; the RR intervals vary irregularly between 0.35 and 0.65 s and no organised P waves are present, so there is no measurable PR interval. QRS 102 ms, QT 291 ms, QTc 451 ms. Axis about +1 degree (normal). The earlier ECG the same day (2026-06-10 17:13) showed the same irregularly irregular rhythm at 139 bpm (QTc 446 ms), so atrial fibrillation is not new on this tracing. Note that the clinic note of 2026-06-10 describes normal sinus rhythm at 72 bpm, which both same-day tracings contradict.

Sinus rhythm at 98 bpm with upright P waves. PR about 175 ms, QRS 80 ms, QT 323 ms, QTc 413 ms. Axis about +38 degrees (normal). No bundle branch block or AV block. Prior ECG 2021-04-20 was sinus at 81 bpm with QTc 393 ms; no change in rhythm, conduction or QTc.

Sinus bradycardia at 58 bpm with a discrete P wave before each QRS; PR about 196 ms (upper normal, no AV block). QRS 94 ms. QT 546 ms with QTc (Bazett) 535 ms - markedly prolonged, in a patient on amiodarone. Axis about +19 degrees (normal). The prior ECG of 2022-04-06 showed atrial fibrillation with a rapid, irregularly irregular ventricular response at 131 bpm and no P waves, QTc 430 ms; sinus rhythm has been restored (resolved AF) and the QTc has increased by more than 100 ms.

Sinus tachycardia at 107 bpm with a P wave before every QRS; PR about 150 ms, QRS 72 ms, QT 338 ms, QTc 452 ms. Axis about +45 degrees (normal). No bundle branch block. Prior ECG 2019-07-27 was sinus at 75 bpm with QTc 425 ms; no change in rhythm, conduction or QTc (difference 27 ms).

Regular narrow-complex tachycardia at 141 bpm with a perfectly constant RR interval (0.404-0.454 s) and no sinus P waves. QRST-aligned averaging shows continuous organised atrial deflections recurring every 210 ms (atrial rate about 286/min, visible in II, III, aVF and V1) - atrial flutter with 2:1 conduction. No measurable PR interval. QRS 86 ms, QT 274 ms, QTc 420 ms. Axis about +4 degrees (normal). The prior ECG of 2022-07-11 showed atrial fibrillation (irregularly irregular, coefficient of variation 0.24, no P waves) at 110 bpm, so the fibrillation has organised into new atrial flutter. QTc essentially unchanged.

The prior ECG of 2022-07-11 showed atrial fibrillation (irregularly irregular, coefficient of variation 0.24, no P waves) at 110 bpm, so the fibrillation has organised into new atrial flutter. QTc essentially unchanged.

arguments.explanation: Regular rhythm at 69 bpm with a reproducible atrial deflection before every QRS and a PR of about 138 ms - sinus rhythm. QRS 94 ms, QT 355 ms, QTc 382 ms. The frontal plane axis computed from leads I and aVF is about -175 degrees, i.e. an extreme (northwest) axis: lead I shows a deep S wave and aVR is dominantly positive while the praecordial R wave progression is normal, a pattern that strongly suggests right/left arm lead reversal rather than true dextrocardia - the limb lead placement should be checked. No bundle branch block or AV block. Only ECG for this patient; no prior comparison.

Sinus rhythm at 91 bpm with consistent P waves. PR about 185 ms (within normal limits), QRS 84 ms, QT 338 ms, QTc 416 ms. Axis about +2 degrees (normal). No bundle branch block. Prior ECG 2021-05-16 was sinus at 87 bpm, PR 136 ms, QTc 397 ms; no categorical change.

Sinus tachycardia at 112 bpm; RR intervals are essentially constant and a reproducible P wave (positive in II, negative in V1) precedes each QRS with a PR of about 180 ms. QRS 98 ms, QT 295 ms, QTc 402 ms, with ST depression and T wave inversion inferolaterally. Axis about +40 degrees (normal). Prior ECG 2022-07-04 was virtually identical (sinus tachycardia 115 bpm, QTc 402 ms); no change.

Sinus rhythm at 68 bpm with upright P waves. PR about 140 ms, QRS 92 ms, QT 478 ms and QTc (Bazett) 509 ms - prolonged, in a patient on escitalopram. Axis about +46 degrees (normal). No bundle branch block or AV block. The prior ECG of 2022-11-23 was sinus at 74 bpm with QTc 357 ms, so the QTc has increased by about 150 ms.

Sinus rhythm at 70 bpm with a P wave before each QRS. PR about 155 ms, QRS 106 ms (nonspecific intraventricular conduction delay, not meeting bundle branch block criteria), QT 494 ms and QTc (Bazett) 534 ms - markedly prolonged in a patient on citalopram 40 mg daily. Axis about +40 degrees (normal). The prior ECG of 2020-06-17 showed sinus tachycardia at 132 bpm with a rightward axis and QTc 461 ms; the QTc has increased by more than 60 ms.

Sinus rhythm at 66 bpm with consistent P waves; occasional slight RR variation only. PR 162 ms, QRS 98 ms, QT 353 ms, QTc 370 ms. Frontal axis about -51 degrees, i.e. left axis deviation (left anterior fascicular pattern) with deep S waves in II, III, aVF and V6. No bundle branch block. Prior ECG 2024-02-01 was also sinus with left axis deviation and QTc 396 ms; no change.

Sinus tachycardia at 121 bpm with regular RR intervals and a P wave before each QRS. PR 126 ms, QRS 90 ms, QT 302 ms, QTc 429 ms. Axis about +62 degrees (normal). No conduction abnormality. This is the patient's only ECG, so no comparison is possible.

Sinus tachycardia at 109 bpm with upright P waves. PR 116 ms, QRS 92 ms, QT 351 ms, QTc 475 ms (prolonged for rate). Axis about +34 degrees (normal). No bundle branch block or AV block. Only ECG available; no prior for comparison.
Sinus rhythm at 97 bpm with a P wave before every QRS. PR 106 ms, QRS 78 ms, QT 297 ms, QTc 379 ms. Axis about +1 degree (normal). No conduction abnormality. Single ECG; no prior comparison.

Irregularly irregular narrow-complex tachycardia at a mean rate of 145 bpm (RR 0.36-0.55 s) with no organised P activity - atrial fibrillation with rapid ventricular response. Sinus rhythm at 77 bpm with consistent P waves. PR 150 ms, QRS 76 ms, QT 400 ms, QTc 452 ms (mildly prolonged). Axis about +67 degrees (normal). No conduction block. Sinus rhythm at 101 bpm with clear P waves. PR 140 ms, QRS 94 ms, QT 321 ms, QTc 417 ms. Axis about +59 degrees (normal). No conduction abnormality. The prior tracing was recorded one minute earlier the same day and is essentially identical (101 bpm, QTc 416 ms); no change.

Sinus rhythm at 98 bpm with upright P waves. PR about 175 ms, QRS 80 ms, QT 323 ms, QTc 413 ms. Axis about +38 degrees (normal). No bundle branch block or AV block. Prior ECG 2021-04-20 was sinus at 81 bpm with QTc 393 ms; no change in rhythm, conduction or QTc.

QTc essentially unchanged.

Sinus tachycardia at 112 bpm; RR intervals are essentially constant and a reproducible P wave (positive in II, negative in V1) precedes each QRS with a PR of about 180 ms. Sinus rhythm at 68 bpm with upright P waves. PR about 140 ms, QRS 92 ms, QT 478 ms and QTc (Bazett) 509 ms - prolonged, in a patient on escitalopram. Axis about +46 degrees (normal). Sinus rhythm at 70 bpm with a P wave before each QRS. Sinus rhythm at 66 bpm with consistent P waves; occasional slight RR variation only. PR 162 ms, QRS 98 ms, QT 353 ms, QTc 370 ms. Sinus tachycardia at 121 bpm with regular RR intervals and a P wave before each QRS. PR 126 ms, QRS 90 ms, QT 302 ms, QTc 429 ms. Axis about +62 degrees (normal). No conduction abnormality. This is the patient's only ECG, so no comparison is possible.

Sinus tachycardia at 109 bpm with upright P waves. PR 116 ms, QRS 92 ms, QT 351 ms, QTc 475 ms (prolonged for rate). Axis about +34 degrees (normal). No bundle branch block or AV block. Only ECG available; no prior for comparison.
Sinus rhythm at 97 bpm with a P wave before every QRS. PR 106 ms, QRS 78 ms, QT 297 ms, QTc 379 ms. Axis about +1 degree (normal). No conduction abnormality. Single ECG; no prior comparison.

Atrial fibrillation with rapid ventricular response, mean rate 139 bpm; RR intervals are irregularly irregular and no P waves are identifiable on signal-averaged analysis. No measurable PR interval. The prior ECG of 2024-08-18 also showed atrial fibrillation at 132 bpm (QTc 461 ms), consistent with the documented chronic atrial fibrillation; no change.

Atrial fibrillation with a slow, markedly irregular ventricular response, mean rate 53 bpm (RMSSD 0.44 s); no P waves are present and there is no measurable PR interval. Sinus bradycardia at 52 bpm with a P wave before every QRS. PR 166 ms, QRS 94 ms, QT 417 ms, QTc 388 ms. Axis about +33 degrees (normal). No bundle branch block. Prior ECG 2023-05-22 was sinus at 57 bpm with QTc 346 ms; no categorical change (QTc difference 42 ms).

Atrial fibrillation at a mean ventricular rate of 87 bpm; irregularly irregular RR intervals with absent P waves and no measurable PR interval. QRS 92 ms, QT 369 ms, QTc 444 ms. QTc difference 46 ms, not a reportable change.

Sinus rhythm at 74 bpm with a P wave before every QRS. PR 180 ms, QRS 90 ms, QT 381 ms, QTc 423 ms. Axis about +35 degrees (normal). No bundle branch block or AV block. Only ECG for this patient; no prior comparison.

The prior ECG of 2020-11-03 was also a regular wide-complex (196 ms) rhythm without P waves at 109 bpm, i.e. already paced, so there is no new paced rhythm and the QTc is unchanged.

Sinus tachycardia at 102 bpm with a P wave before every QRS. PR 132 ms, QRS 94 ms, QT 338 ms, QTc 440 ms. Axis about +40 degrees (normal). No conduction abnormality. Prior ECG 2025-03-18 was essentially identical (102 bpm, QTc 433 ms); no change.

Sinus rhythm at 101 bpm with clear P waves. PR 140 ms, QRS 94 ms, QT 321 ms, QTc 417 ms. Axis about +59 degrees (normal). No conduction abnormality. The prior tracing was recorded one minute earlier the same day and is essentially identical (101 bpm, QTc 416 ms); no change.

Sinus rhythm at 98 bpm with upright P waves. PR about 175 ms, QRS 80 ms, QT 323 ms, QTc 413 ms. Axis about +38 degrees (normal). No bundle branch block or AV block. Prior ECG 2021-04-20 was sinus at 81 bpm with QTc 393 ms; no change in rhythm, conduction or QTc.

Regular narrow-complex tachycardia at 141 bpm with a perfectly constant RR interval (0.404-0.454 s) and no sinus P waves. QRST-aligned averaging shows continuous organised atrial deflections recurring every 210 ms (atrial rate about 286/min, visible in II, III, aVF and V1) - atrial flutter with 2:1 conduction. No measurable PR interval. QRS 86 ms, QT 274 ms, QTc 420 ms. Axis about +4 degrees (normal). The prior ECG of 2022-07-11 showed atrial fibrillation (irregularly irregular, coefficient of variation 0.24, no P waves) at 110 bpm, so the fibrillation has organised into new atrial flutter. QTc essentially unchanged.

Sinus rhythm at 91 bpm with consistent P waves. PR about 185 ms (within normal limits), QRS 84 ms, QT 338 ms, QTc 416 ms. Axis about +2 degrees (normal). No bundle branch block. Prior ECG 2021-05-16 was sinus at 87 bpm, PR 136 ms, QTc 397 ms; no categorical change.

Sinus tachycardia at 112 bpm; RR intervals are essentially constant and a reproducible P wave (positive in II, negative in V1) precedes each QRS with a PR of about 180 ms. QRS 98 ms, QT 295 ms, QTc 402 ms, with ST depression and T wave inversion inferolaterally. Axis about +40 degrees (normal). Prior ECG 2022-07-04 was virtually identical (sinus tachycardia 115 bpm, QTc 402 ms); no change.

Sinus rhythm at 68 bpm with upright P waves. PR about 140 ms, QRS 92 ms, QT 478 ms and QTc (Bazett) 509 ms - prolonged, in a patient on escitalopram. Axis about +46 degrees (normal). No bundle branch block or AV block. The prior ECG of 2022-11-23 was sinus at 74 bpm with QTc 357 ms, so the QTc has increased by about 150 ms.

Sinus rhythm at 70 bpm with a P wave before each QRS. PR about 155 ms, QRS 106 ms (nonspecific intraventricular conduction delay, not meeting bundle branch block criteria), QT 494 ms and QTc (Bazett) 534 ms - markedly prolonged in a patient on citalopram 40 mg daily. Axis about +40 degrees (normal). The prior ECG of 2020-06-17 showed sinus tachycardia at 132 bpm with a rightward axis and QTc 461 ms; the QTc has increased by more than 60 ms.

Sinus rhythm at 66 bpm with consistent P waves; occasional slight RR variation only. PR 162 ms, QRS 98 ms, QT 353 ms, QTc 370 ms. Frontal axis about -51 degrees, i.e. left axis deviation (left anterior fascicular pattern) with deep S waves in II, III, aVF and V6. No bundle branch block. Prior ECG 2024-02-01 was also sinus with left axis deviation and QTc 396 ms; no change.

Sinus tachycardia at 121 bpm with regular RR intervals and a P wave before each QRS. PR 126 ms, QRS 90 ms, QT 302 ms, QTc 429 ms. Axis about +62 degrees (normal). No conduction abnormality. This is the patient's only ECG, so no comparison is possible.

Sinus tachycardia at 109 bpm with upright P waves. PR 116 ms, QRS 92 ms, QT 351 ms, QTc 475 ms (prolonged for rate). Axis about +34 degrees (normal). No bundle branch block or AV block. Only ECG available; no prior for comparison.
Sinus rhythm at 97 bpm with a P wave before every QRS. PR 106 ms, QRS 78 ms, QT 297 ms, QTc 379 ms. Axis about +1 degree (normal). No conduction abnormality. Single ECG; no prior comparison.

Irregularly irregular narrow-complex tachycardia at a mean rate of 145 bpm (RR 0.36-0.55 s) with no organised P activity - atrial fibrillation with rapid ventricular response. No measurable PR interval. QRS 102 ms, QT 288 ms, QTc 447 ms. Axis about -16 degrees (normal). The prior ECG of 2024-06-25 showed sinus rhythm at 81 bpm with PR 176 ms, so atrial fibrillation is new. QTc unchanged (difference 24 ms).

Sinus rhythm at 61 bpm. PR about 212 ms, i.e. first-degree AV block. QRS 134 ms with a broad monophasic R wave in I, aVL and V6 (no septal q, no S wave in V6) and a deep QS complex in V1-V3 - left bundle branch block. QT 445 ms, QTc 449 ms. Axis about -25 degrees (normal). The prior ECG of 2024-06-03 showed the same sinus rhythm with PR 218 ms and LBBB with QRS 134 ms, so neither the bundle branch block nor the AV block is new and the QTc is unchanged.

Sinus rhythm at 77 bpm with consistent P waves. PR 150 ms, QRS 76 ms, QT 400 ms, QTc 452 ms (mildly prolonged). Axis about +67 degrees (normal). No conduction block. Prior ECG 2020-02-02 was also sinus at 75 bpm with a low-amplitude inverted T wave and QTc 511 ms; the QTc has shortened by 59 ms, just short of the 60 ms threshold, so no change is reported.

Atrial fibrillation with rapid ventricular response, mean rate 139 bpm; RR intervals are irregularly irregular and no P waves are identifiable on signal-averaged analysis. No measurable PR interval. QRS 94 ms, QT 296 ms, QTc 450 ms. Axis about -12 degrees (normal). The prior ECG of 2024-08-18 also showed atrial fibrillation at 132 bpm (QTc 461 ms), consistent with the documented chronic atrial fibrillation; no change.

Atrial fibrillation with a slow, markedly irregular ventricular response, mean rate 53 bpm (RMSSD 0.44 s); no P waves are present and there is no measurable PR interval. QRS 112 ms (nonspecific intraventricular conduction delay). QT 385 ms, QTc 360 ms. Frontal axis about -36 degrees (left axis deviation). The prior ECG of 2024-09-04 also showed atrial fibrillation (81 bpm, QRS 116 ms, QTc 419 ms); no categorical change (QTc difference 59 ms, below the 60 ms threshold).

Atrial fibrillation at a mean ventricular rate of 99 bpm: the RR intervals are irregularly irregular (coefficient of variation 0.29) and no P waves can be identified, so there is no measurable PR interval. QRS 86 ms, QT 323 ms, QTc 415 ms. Frontal axis about -49 degrees (left axis deviation). This is the patient's only ECG; atrial fibrillation was coded at the same admission.

Sinus bradycardia at 52 bpm with a P wave before every QRS. PR 166 ms, QRS 94 ms, QT 417 ms, QTc 388 ms. Axis about +33 degrees (normal). No bundle branch block. Prior ECG 2023-05-22 was sinus at 57 bpm with QTc 346 ms; no categorical change (QTc difference 42 ms).

Atrial fibrillation at a mean ventricular rate of 87 bpm; irregularly irregular RR intervals with absent P waves and no measurable PR interval. QRS 92 ms, QT 369 ms, QTc 444 ms. Axis about +25 degrees (normal). The prior ECG of 2024-10-30 also showed atrial fibrillation at 65 bpm (QTc 433 ms); no change.

Atrial fibrillation with a slow irregular ventricular response, mean rate 53 bpm; no P waves and no measurable PR interval. QRS 92 ms, QT 414 ms, QTc 389 ms. Axis about +24 degrees (normal). The prior ECG of 2024-11-12 showed sinus rhythm at 69 bpm with PR 174 ms and clear P waves, so atrial fibrillation is new. QTc unchanged.

Sinus tachycardia at 121 bpm with constant RR intervals and a P wave before each QRS. PR 126 ms, QRS 92 ms (now narrow), QT 302 ms, QTc 430 ms. Frontal axis about +110 degrees (right axis deviation). The earlier ECG the same day (2024-12-05 01:33) showed a markedly widened QRS of 170 ms with a tall broad R wave in V1-V2 and terminal S waves in I and V6, i.e. right bundle branch block; this has resolved on the later tracing. QTc difference 46 ms, not a reportable change.

Irregularly irregular wide-complex rhythm at a mean rate of 96 bpm with no P waves and no pacing artefact - atrial fibrillation conducted with a marked intraventricular conduction delay (QRS about 160 ms, broad R in I and V6 with deep S in V1-V2). No measurable PR interval. QT 352 ms, QTc 445 ms. Axis about -17 degrees (normal). The prior ECG of 2024-12-03 (pacemaker check encounter) showed a regular wide-complex rhythm at 79 bpm with no atrial activity and no rate variation, i.e. ventricular paced rhythm; the current tracing shows intrinsically conducted atrial fibrillation, so the paced rhythm has resolved and atrial fibrillation is new.

Atrial fibrillation with rapid ventricular response at a mean rate of 152 bpm; irregularly irregular RR intervals with absent P waves and no measurable PR interval. QRS 86 ms, QT 290 ms, QTc 461 ms. Axis about +60 degrees (normal). The prior ECG of 2025-01-06 showed sinus rhythm at 86 bpm with PR 118 ms and perfectly regular RR intervals, so atrial fibrillation is new. QTc unchanged.

Sinus rhythm at 74 bpm with a P wave before every QRS. PR 180 ms, QRS 90 ms, QT 381 ms, QTc 423 ms. Axis about +35 degrees (normal). No bundle branch block or AV block. Only ECG for this patient; no prior comparison.

Regular wide-complex rhythm at 111 bpm with no discernible P activity and sharp high-frequency pacing artefacts immediately preceding every QRS (present in 100 percent of beats) - ventricular paced rhythm; the patient has a pacemaker/ICD in situ. No measurable PR interval. QRS 152 ms, QT 399 ms, QTc 543 ms. Frontal axis about +135 degrees (right). Conduction abnormalities are not separately reported because the wide QRS is pacemaker-generated. The prior ECG of 2020-11-03 was also a regular wide-complex (196 ms) rhythm without P waves at 109 bpm, i.e. already paced, so there is no new paced rhythm and the QTc is unchanged.

Sinus tachycardia at 111 bpm: the RR intervals are almost perfectly constant (0.51-0.55 s) and a small but reproducible upright P wave precedes each QRS with a PR of about 128 ms. QRS 78 ms, QT 297 ms, QTc 404 ms. Axis about +54 degrees (normal). The prior ECG a few hours earlier (2025-03-07 19:50) showed the same regular sinus tachycardia at 116 bpm (QTc 369 ms); no change.

Sinus bradycardia at 58 bpm with clear P waves. PR 108 ms, QRS 90 ms, QT 426 ms, QTc 420 ms. Axis about +57 degrees (normal). No conduction abnormality. Prior ECG 2025-03-08 was essentially identical (sinus 62 bpm, PR 108 ms, QTc 439 ms); no change.

Sinus rhythm at a baseline rate of 61 bpm with a single early beat and compensatory pause (RR 0.98, 0.98, 0.54, 1.37, 0.99 s); apart from this ectopic beat the rhythm is regular with a reproducible P wave (upright in II, negative terminal component in V1) before every QRS, so this is sinus rhythm with an atrial premature complex rather than atrial fibrillation. PR about 180 ms, QRS 104 ms, QT 388 ms, QTc 392 ms. Axis about -23 degrees (normal). Only ECG available; paroxysmal atrial fibrillation was coded clinically at this admission but is not captured on this tracing.

Sinus tachycardia at 102 bpm with a P wave before every QRS. PR 132 ms, QRS 94 ms, QT 338 ms, QTc 440 ms. Axis about +40 degrees (normal). No conduction abnormality. Prior ECG 2025-03-18 was essentially identical (102 bpm, QTc 433 ms); no change.

Sinus tachycardia at 120 bpm; regular RR intervals with a consistent P wave merging into the preceding T wave. PR about 190 ms, QRS 98 ms, QT 280 ms, QTc 397 ms. Axis about +40 degrees (normal). No bundle branch block. The prior ECG of 2016-09-16 was also sinus tachycardia (108 bpm, QTc 396 ms); no change.

Sinus rhythm at 101 bpm with clear P waves. PR 140 ms, QRS 94 ms, QT 321 ms, QTc 417 ms. Axis about +59 degrees (normal). No conduction abnormality. The prior tracing was recorded one minute earlier the same day and is essentially identical (101 bpm, QTc 416 ms); no change.

Sinus rhythm at 98 bpm with upright P waves. PR about 175 ms, QRS 80 ms, QT 323 ms, QTc 413 ms. Axis about +38 degrees (normal). No bundle branch block or AV block. Prior ECG 2021-04-20 was sinus at 81 bpm with QTc 393 ms; no change in rhythm, conduction or QTc.

Sinus bradycardia at 58 bpm with a discrete P wave before each QRS; PR about 196 ms (upper normal, no AV block). QRS 94 ms. QT 546 ms with QTc (Bazett) 535 ms - markedly prolonged, in a patient on amiodarone. Axis about +19 degrees (normal). The prior ECG of 2022-04-06 showed atrial fibrillation with a rapid, irregularly irregular ventricular response at 131 bpm and no P waves, QTc 430 ms; sinus rhythm has been restored (resolved AF) and the QTc has increased by more than 100 ms.

Sinus tachycardia at 107 bpm with a P wave before every QRS; PR about 150 ms, QRS 72 ms, QT 338 ms, QTc 452 ms. Axis about +45 degrees (normal). No bundle branch block. Prior ECG 2019-07-27 was sinus at 75 bpm with QTc 425 ms; no change in rhythm, conduction or QTc (difference 27 ms).

Regular narrow-complex tachycardia at 141 bpm with a perfectly constant RR interval (0.404-0.454 s) and no sinus P waves. QRST-aligned averaging shows continuous organised atrial deflections recurring every 210 ms (atrial rate about 286/min, visible in II, III, aVF and V1) - atrial flutter with 2:1 conduction. No measurable PR interval. QRS 86 ms, QT 274 ms, QTc 420 ms. Axis about +4 degrees (normal). The prior ECG of 2022-07-11 showed atrial fibrillation (irregularly irregular, coefficient of variation 0.24, no P waves) at 110 bpm, so the fibrillation has organised into new atrial flutter. QTc essentially unchanged.

items.explanation: 71-year-old man with atrial fibrillation documented 2025-08-22 (ICD-9 427.31). CHA2DS2-VASc 3 (hypertension, age 65-74, vascular disease: coronary atherosclerosis of native coronary artery). No anticoagulant in any current order or clinic medication list (most recent cardiology clinic note 2026-07-28 lists tamsulosin only). Guideline-recommended oral anticoagulation is absent.

Most recent ECG (101515306, 2022-04-27) shows sinus bradycardia at 58 bpm with QT 546 ms, QTc (Bazett) 535 ms. Amiodarone 200 mg daily is a QT watch-list medication and is current (order 2026-08-22, valid to 2027-01-05). Most recent potassium 4.1 mEq/L and magnesium 1.8 mg/dL (both 2026-02-14). QTc >= 500 ms on a watch-list drug requires prescriber review; no ECG has been obtained since 2022 despite continuing amiodarone.

Amiodarone 200 mg daily (a QT watch-list medication) was started at the cardiology clinic visit of 2025-11-10; it first appears in that visit's medication list. The 9/1/2025 memo applies (start before 3/1/2026), so an ECG was required within 30 days, i.e. by 2025-12-10. ECG 106885519 was obtained 2025-11-24, 14 days after the start, so the requirement was met.

Escitalopram 10 mg daily (QT watch-list) was started at the cardiology clinic visit of 2026-02-12 (first order and first appearance in the medication list). Start was before 3/1/2026, so the 30-day window of the 9/1/2025 memo applies: ECG due by 2026-03-14. ECG 101538691 was obtained 2026-03-08, 24 days after the start, so the requirement was met.

Citalopram 40 mg daily (QT watch-list) was started at the cardiology clinic visit of 2026-03-02; it is absent from the 2025-12-15 medication list and present from 2026-03-02. Start on/after 3/1/2026, so the revised memo applies: ECG required within 14 days, by 2026-03-16. ECG 104882441 was obtained at the 2026-03-07 visit, 5 days after the start, so the requirement was met.

Escitalopram 10 mg daily (QT watch-list) was started at the cardiology clinic visit of 2026-04-10. Start on/after 3/1/2026, so an ECG was required within 14 days, by 2026-04-24. The only ECG (107859369) was recorded 2026-04-29, 19 days after the start and 5 days after the deadline, so the monitoring was not completed within the required time.

Escitalopram 10 mg daily (QT watch-list) was started at the cardiology clinic visit of 2026-08-01; it is absent from the 2026-06-24 medication list. An ECG was required within 14 days, by 2026-08-15. The patient's only ECG is from 2025-12-25, before the start, and no ECG has been obtained since; the deadline has passed.

Escitalopram 10 mg daily (QT watch-list) was started at the cardiology clinic visit of 2026-08-10, so an ECG was required by 2026-08-24. The telephone note of 2026-08-25 records that the patient had an ECG at Northside Urgent Care on 8/18 (within the window) but the report was requested by fax and has not been received; there is no ECG for this patient in the chart. The outside tracing could have satisfied the requirement, so completion cannot be determined until the report arrives.

Haloperidol 2 mg twice daily (QT watch-list) was started at the cardiology clinic visit of 2026-09-15. Under the revised memo an ECG is required within 14 days, i.e. by 2026-09-29. No ECG has been obtained since the start (last ECG 2025-03-09), but the deadline is after the evaluation date of 2026-09-24, so the monitoring is not yet due.

At the cardiology clinic visit of 2026-09-01 Dr. Kessler documented a warfarin dose increase from 5 mg to 7.5 mg daily for a subtherapeutic INR of 1.6. The 3/1/2026 memo requires an INR within 7 days of a dose change made by a clinic clinician, i.e. by 2026-09-08. INR 2.3 was resulted on 2026-09-05, within the window, so the requirement was met.

Anticoagulation clinic telephone note of 2026-09-10 by the clinic pharmacist documents warfarin decreased from 5 mg to 4 mg daily per protocol for a home INR of 3.4. The 3/1/2026 memo requires a confirmatory INR within 7 days of a pharmacist dose change, i.e. by 2026-09-17. The most recent INR in the chart is 2.6 from 2026-08-22, before the change, and no INR has been resulted since; the deadline passed before the 2026-09-24 evaluation.

71-year-old woman with paroxysmal atrial fibrillation documented 2025-03-14 (ICD-10 I48.0) at the same admission as an embolic cerebral infarction. CHA2DS2-VASc 5: prior stroke (2), hypertension (1), age 65-74 (1), female sex (1). No anticoagulant is ordered; cardiology clinic notes through 2026-07-10 list only famotidine, metoprolol and carvedilol. Guideline-recommended oral anticoagulation is absent.

Outside-records summary of 2026-08-12 documents an admission 8/2/2026-8/5/2026 for upper GI bleeding from a duodenal ulcer (haemoglobin nadir 6.9, 2 units transfused) with apixaban held at discharge pending cardiology review. Nevertheless apixaban 5 mg twice daily was re-ordered at the 2026-08-20 cardiology clinic visit (valid 2026-08-20 to 2026-12-28) and is current, alongside aspirin and clopidogrel. Anticoagulation should not continue without the documented cardiology review of the recent major GI bleed.

At the 2026-07-15 cardiology clinic visit the plan was to switch from rivaroxaban to apixaban, but apixaban 5 mg twice daily (valid 2026-07-15 to 2026-12-26) was started while the rivaroxaban 20 mg daily order (valid 2026-07-15 to 2026-12-25) was left active; the visit medication list shows both. Two oral anticoagulants are therefore current as of 2026-09-24.

Cardiology clinic note of 2026-06-10 states 'ECG obtained today: normal sinus rhythm, rate 72'. Both 12-lead ECGs recorded the same day (107914094 at 17:13 and 103088543 at 19:36) show an irregularly irregular ventricular response with no discernible P waves at 139 and 144 bpm, i.e. atrial fibrillation with rapid ventricular response. Unspecified atrial fibrillation was also coded for the 2026-06-10 encounter. The documented rhythm and rate are contradicted by the same-day ECGs.

Heart-rate-rhythm observation of 2022-04-06 06:38 records 'Normal Sinus Rhythm'. The 12-lead ECG obtained the same day at 06:30 (100867733) shows an irregularly irregular rhythm (RR 0.32-0.62 s) without P waves at 131 bpm, i.e. atrial fibrillation; atrial fibrillation was also recorded four minutes earlier (06:34) and coded for that encounter. The sinus-rhythm documentation is contradicted by the same-day ECG.

Most recent ECG (108018814, 2023-10-08) shows sinus rhythm at 68 bpm with QT 478 ms, QTc (Bazett) 509 ms. Escitalopram 10 mg daily is a QT watch-list medication and is current (order 2026-04-23, valid to 2027-01-02). Most recent potassium 4.1 mEq/L and magnesium 2.1 mg/dL (both 2025-08-23) are normal. Per the 1/15/2025 QT monitoring memo a most recent ECG with QTc >= 500 ms on a watch-list drug requires prescriber review.

Most recent ECG (104821039, 2023-11-10) shows sinus rhythm at 70 bpm with QT 494 ms, QTc (Bazett) 534 ms. Citalopram 40 mg daily (a QT watch-list medication, and a dose above the 20 mg maximum advised with QT risk) is current (order 2026-05-29, valid to 2026-12-25). Most recent potassium 4.5 mEq/L (2026-01-21) and magnesium 2.1 mg/dL (2023-12-01). QTc >= 500 ms on a watch-list drug requires prescriber review.

Most recent ECG (106885519, 2025-11-24) shows sinus rhythm at 62 bpm with QT 514 ms, QTc (Bazett) 523 ms, up from 413 ms on the prior ECG of 2025-06-07. Amiodarone 200 mg daily is a QT watch-list medication and is current (order 2026-07-29, valid to 2027-01-05). Most recent potassium 4.4 mEq/L and magnesium 2.2 mg/dL (both 2026-04-20) are normal. QTc >= 500 ms on a watch-list drug requires prescriber review.

Sinus rhythm at 70 bpm with a P wave before each QRS. Sinus rhythm at 83 bpm with a P wave before every QRS. PR 140 ms, QRS 80 ms, QT 347 ms, QTc 409 ms. Axis about +51 degrees (normal). No conduction abnormality. Only ECG for this patient; no prior comparison.

Sinus rhythm at 66 bpm with consistent P waves. PR 152 ms, QRS 94 ms, QT 370 ms, QTc 387 ms. Axis about -27 degrees (normal). No bundle branch block or AV block. Only ECG for this patient; no prior comparison.
